narrative.summary: ICESCO's one AI instrument found so far is the Riyadh Charter on Artificial Intelligence for the Islamic World, published in 2025 in Arabic, English and French and developed with Saudi Arabia's SDAIA. It sets ethical principles for the design, conduct and governance of AI grounded in Islamic values, recommends impact assessments, a trustworthy-AI quality label and national regulatory frameworks, and closes with an implementation roadmap. It is a non-binding declaration of intent. Its formal adoption by ICESCO's governing bodies is reported in ICESCO news but not yet confirmed from a decision document.
narrative.review_notes: ICESCO's own site (icesco.org) was searched for AI charters, declarations and strategies. The member list comes from ICESCO's member-states page, as the older isesco.org address no longer serves it. Observer states are not listed. Pending: the decision text recording the Charter's adoption, and texts for the AI Index and ministerial declarations known only from news. The Charter is published by ICESCO in Arabic, English and French; the record uses the Arabic title and links the Arabic and English PDFs. The text does not state which language version is authentic.

instruments.current_status: Published by ICESCO in Arabic, English and French; the cover and title page print only '2025'. The text calls itself 'a shared vision, a declaration of intent, and a guiding compass' and has no signature or ratification mechanism. Its preamble recalls the Executive Council's 43rd session (2022, Rabat), which asked ICESCO to prepare the Charter, and 44th session (2024, Jeddah), and expects its adoption by the Executive Council and the General Conference. That adoption is not yet confirmed from an official decision document, so it is recorded as published, not adopted. Developed with the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA). The English version (source_url) and the Arabic version (official_pdf_url, ICESCO's June 2026 reissue) are both ICESCO publications; the text does not state which language version is authentic.
instruments.summary: This 40-page ethical and strategic framework is written as a declaration by 'the Governments of the Member States'. It sets out preconditions for AI development and three groups of principles: ethical design (human dignity, personal sovereignty, truth and authenticity, solidarity, privacy, fairness and inclusion, well-being, trustworthiness), ethical conduct (prudence, responsibility) and ethical governance (human oversight, accountability, redress and compensation for harm), all grounded in Islamic values. It makes recommendations to Member States and ICESCO, including ex ante and ex post impact assessments, a quality label for trustworthy AI, regulatory frameworks, green AI and capacity building, and closes with a strategic implementation roadmap that includes national ethical frameworks, risk classification, an AI readiness index and an annual AI ministers' conference.
